findings.highlight: I’m the only one who can move
findings.evidenceJa: 満足に動けるのは俺だけだ
findings.governingReading: Shirou alone can still move properly or freely.
findings.explanation: The English erases the qualification that the others are not wholly immobile but cannot move effectively.

findings.highlight: I just need to get the main cause
findings.evidenceJa: その元凶さえ叩いてしまえば
findings.governingReading: He only needs to strike the source of the problem.
findings.explanation: The English omits the planned attack and produces an unclear “get the main cause.”

findings.governingReading: Are you in your right mind?
findings.explanation: Archer’s alarm at Shirou’s suicidal choice becomes a flat insult to his intelligence.
The specific tactical constraint of width becomes generic smallness.

findings.highlight: if Archer fell to the ground
findings.evidenceJa: アーチャーが砕け落ちたとしても
findings.governingReading: even if Archer shattered and fell apart
findings.explanation: The petrification’s destructive result is reduced to an ordinary fall.

findings.evidenceJa: いずれ心も硬化するだろう
findings.governingReading: Eventually his mind too will harden.
findings.explanation: The English changes eventual mental petrification into an immediately rapid process.
